description: Shelter staff need to complete intake records for newly arrived animals when names, ages, prior histories, and health status are uncertain or partially unknown. All shelter and animal names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 32-year-old intake coordinator at a busy municipal shelter
user_profile.context: Animals are arriving faster than perfect histories can be gathered, but the records still need to support later care and placement
user_profile.communication_style: Compassionate and structured, wants uncertainty documented instead of guessed away

fact_sheet.fact: The standard intake form for a new animal is Form 77B, which must be initiated within 15 minutes of the animal's arrival at Oak Valley Animal Haven.
The shelter's management software, 'ShelterPaws Pro', is accessed via the URL https://ovah.shelterpawspro.net.
Upon intake, each animal is assigned a temporary ID collar; canines receive blue collars and felines receive green collars.
All incoming canines over 6 months old receive a 1 mL dose of Bordetella vaccine administered intranasally.
For any urgent medical concerns during intake, the on-call veterinarian, Dr. Aris Thorne, must be paged at extension 55.
The primary animal intake processing room is designated as 'Intake Suite A', located next to the main lobby.
A male German Shepherd mix, admitted on May 16, 2024, was assigned the temporary ID '24-0516-D01' due to having no name or microchip.
In ShelterPaws Pro, if an animal's age is unknown, the 'Date of Birth' field should be left blank and the 'Age Estimate' field must be filled with a value like 'Approx. 2 years'.
A high-resolution photograph of the animal's face and full body must be uploaded to its profile in ShelterPaws Pro within one hour of intake.
All felines are treated for fleas upon arrival with a topical application of selamectin dosed at 6 mg/kg.
Permanent microchips (brand: HomeAgain) are implanted between the shoulder blades by a vet tech during the initial health screening.
A litter of four kittens, case ID '24-0515-F03', arrived without a mother and their health status was marked as 'Requires Neonatal Monitoring' in their records.
Jenna Carter, the Intake Coordinator, works at workstation #3 in the main administrative office and can be reached at j.carter@ovahaven.org.
All newly arrived animals with unknown vaccination histories are housed in the Quarantine Wing (Kennel Block Q) for a minimum of 10 days.
To indicate an unknown history, the 'Intake Subtype' dropdown in ShelterPaws Pro should be set to 'Stray - Unknown Origin'.
Puppies and kittens under 4 months are administered Pyrantel Pamoate for deworming at a dosage of 5 mg/kg, with a follow-up dose in 2 weeks.
If an animal is surrendered with personal items like a blanket or toy, these items must be labeled with the animal's temporary ID and stored in Bin 27.
The cat 'Luna', ID '24-0514-F02', was admitted with partial vet records indicating a spay surgery in 2021 but no vaccination history since 2022.
Daily intake summary reports are automatically generated by ShelterPaws Pro at 8:00 PM and posted to the #intake-reports Slack channel.
A record can be flagged for 'Behavioral Assessment' by checking the corresponding box under the 'Status Flags' tab in the animal's profile.
The shelter's walk-in refrigerator for storing temperature-sensitive medications like vaccines is kept at a constant 38°F (3.3°C).
A SNAP 4Dx test is performed on all canines over 6 months of age to screen for heartworm, Lyme, anaplasmosis, and ehrlichiosis.
Any animal showing signs of aggression during intake must have a red 'Caution' tag added to their physical kennel card and digital record.
The animal's permanent ID number is generated by combining the year, intake number, and species code (e.g., 2024-1038-C for a canine).
For cat 'Luna' (ID '24-0514-F02'), a note was added to her record: 'Owner deceased. History provided by neighbor, may be incomplete. Recommend full senior blood panel.'
